claims.claim: The DNS domain name space is a tree structure in which nodes and leaves have associated information.
Resolvers provide applications access to DNS name servers and can use cached data.
A DNS resource record includes an owner name, type, class, TTL, and record data.
RFC 1035 defines A as a host-address record and CNAME as the canonical or primary name for an alias.
The TTL of a resource record specifies the interval for which it may be cached before its source is consulted again.
Within an RRSet, RFC 2181 requires all sent records to have equal TTLs and directs caches to treat unequal TTLs using the lowest value.
DNS supplies naming information, while HTTP defines a separate application-layer request and response model for web resources.

unsupportedExistingClaims: The generated draft consisted of generic boilerplate and made no specific, source-supported claims about DNS.
correctionsNeeded: Replaced generic content with a bounded explanation of DNS names, records, resolvers, caches, and TTL.
Separated DNS lookup from domain registration, HTTP delivery, HTTPS, and hosting.
Used a command-format example without presenting volatile live address data as a durable fact.
Added an explicit warning that a successful DNS answer does not prove a successful web transaction.

sourceRecords.title: RFC 1034 — Domain Names: Concepts and Facilities
sourceRecords.notes: Read directly. Supports the distributed DNS model, the name-space tree, the resolver and name-server roles, and cached resolver data. No source prose reproduced.

sourceRecords.title: RFC 1035 — Domain Names: Implementation and Specification
sourceRecords.notes: Read directly. Supports resource-record fields, the A and CNAME definitions, resolver cache discussion, and the TTL cacheability rule. No source prose reproduced.

sourceRecords.title: RFC 2181 — Clarifications to the DNS Specification
sourceRecords.notes: Read directly. Supports the clarification that records in an RRSet use equal TTLs and cache handling of unequal TTL values. No source prose reproduced.

sourceRecords.title: RFC 9110 — HTTP Semantics
sourceRecords.notes: Existing phase-2 source record reused exactly. Supports the scoped comparison between DNS naming information and the separate HTTP request-response model. No prose reproduced.
